quotes.quote: We used mixed model repeated measures analysis to identify factors affecting body temperatures of cane toads during the 40-min heating trials.
Our measure of climate characteristics at each site (0, 3, 5, or 6 hot dry months per year) was analysed as a continuous variable.

G1.rationale: The principal result is produced by a mixed model repeated measures analysis on body temperature data, which a third party can re-run if the data are available.

G2.rationale: The principal quantitative results are the interaction effects in the mixed model, specifically the climate × water and climate × time interactions, reported in Table 1 with F and P values.

G3.rationale: The deposit listing shows no files, so it is uncertain whether the analysis inputs are deposited.

quotes.quote: Sex and body mass were used as covariates in the analysis with climate at each collection site (# consecutive months per year with average maximum temperature > 30 °C and with < 25 mm rainfall (see above)) and wet/dry treatment as factors and time (0, 20, 40 min) as the repeated measure.
Individual ID nested within population was used as a random effect.

G4.rationale: The method is described in sufficient detail to implement the mixed model repeated measures analysis without the original code.

quotes.quote: and analyses were run using JMP Pro 14.0 (SAS Institute, Cary, NC).

G5.rationale: The analysis used JMP Pro 14.0, which is proprietary software, so the method is not feasible with free software alone.

specification.exact_target: The interactive effect of climate and water treatment on body temperatures of cane toads, reported as F(1,26) = 6.55, P = 0.0166 in Table 1.
specification.blind_target: The interactive effect of climate at collection sites and presence of water during trials on body temperatures of cane toads.

method_quotes.quote: We used mixed model repeated measures analysis to identify factors affecting body temperatures of cane toads during the 40-min heating trials.

Sex and body mass were used as covariates in the analysis with climate at each collection site (# consecutive months per year with average maximum temperature > 30 °C and with < 25 mm rainfall (see above)) and wet/dry treatment as factors and time (0, 20, 40 min) as the repeated measure.
Individual ID nested within population was used as a random effect.
Our measure of climate characteristics at each site (0, 3, 5, or 6 hot dry months per year) was analysed as a continuous variable.

specification.input_notes: The deposit listing for Dryad accession cvdncjt24 shows no files. The data availability statement indicates data are available at 10.5061/dryad.cvdncjt24, but the specific files are not listed.
specification.comparison_metric: The observed F statistic and P value for the climate × water interaction are compared to the reported values.
specification.numerical_agreement_criterion: F statistic within rounding of 6.55 and P value at reported precision (0.0166).
specification.specification_gaps: The exact model specification (e.g., covariance structure, degrees of freedom approximation) is not fully described. The handling of missing data or outliers is not specified.
specification.alternatives_considered: The climate × time interaction (F = 6.44, P = 0.0138) was considered, but the climate × water interaction was chosen as it is the first significant interaction listed in Table 1 and directly addresses the hypothesis about water availability.
